description: Prism and reviewer provider policy. It records temporary freezes, routing principles, and evidence requirements without encoding static model-family bias.
routing_principles: Rank providers by model capability profile plus local CLI stability evidence.
Separate installed/configured visibility from bounded live headless health.
Temporary freezes override ranking because they represent explicit resource or quota constraints.
When a provider is frozen, health probes must report frozen without executing the CLI command.

For long-form analysis, historical archaeology, broad task-tree review and large-document synthesis, prefer Kimi as the primary workload carrier and use Claude Code as cross-check/review unless the task explicitly requires Claude Code's repo-inspection strength.
Copilot CLI is a protected fallback only: Prism, stop-review, live-health, baton delegation and direct RedCap CLI launch may use it only when both Claude Code and Kimi are unavailable.
Codex CLI is a last-resort fallback only: if any non-Codex provider is live-available, normal Prism rosters must suppress Codex.

workload_distribution.scope_note: The workload ratio applies to long-form review and delegation work only; lightweight availability probes, agent detection and direct CLI presence checks are governed by routing_overrides but are not counted as Kimi/Claude long-text workload.

kimi.reason: User requested that Prism workload lean toward Kimi, especially for long-text analysis, while keeping Claude Code as a lower-volume independent reviewer.

claude-code.reason: Claude Code remains important for independent review and repository-aware risk checks, but should not carry the majority of routine long-text Prism workload while Kimi is available.

selection_policy: When both Kimi and Claude Code are available, assign long-form or archaeology-heavy first-pass work to Kimi and reserve Claude Code for cross-check / blocker review.
For two-agent Prism quorum, prefer Kimi + Claude Code with Kimi carrying the larger prompt or first-pass synthesis.

For three-agent or larger Prism runs, keep Kimi at roughly 60-70% of total long-text workload where feasible; use Claude Code for 30-40% and add other providers only when the task benefits from family diversity or Kimi/Claude are unavailable.
This ratio is a workload target, not a quorum replacement; Prism still requires independent evidence and must record resource-limited status when the roster cannot meet policy.
workload_distribution.fallback_policy: If Kimi is unavailable, Claude Code may temporarily carry more work and the run must record the deviation. If Claude Code is unavailable, Kimi may proceed with another available non-protected provider or resource-limited evidence. Copilot and Codex fallback rules remain unchanged.

routing_overrides.reason: User explicitly reserves Copilot CLI quota. RedCap may call Copilot only after Claude Code and Kimi are both unavailable.
User explicitly asked to lower Codex CLI priority and use it only when all other CLI providers are unavailable.

freeze_windows.reason: User explicitly reserved Copilot CLI quota until the monthly freeze window ends.

communication_packet.availability_probe_timeout_policy: Keep availability probes lightweight; the 600 second default applies to real Prism/baton Agent task execution, not to health checks.
communication_packet.raw_output_policy: Keep raw evidence in run-scoped ignored storage when needed; promote only parsed verdict and report summary into tracked evidence.
communication_packet.fallback_policy: If provider quorum cannot be reached without frozen or unhealthy providers, record resource-limited Prism instead of silently weakening the claim.
